findings.title: HSTS is missing or disabled
findings.why: HSTS tells returning browsers to enforce HTTPS. It does not prove origin runtime security.
findings.fix: Set Strict-Transport-Security with a suitable positive max-age after verifying HTTPS across your deployment.

findings.title: HTTP entry point remains unencrypted
evidence: HTTP probe ended at http://example.com/ with status 200.
findings.why: First-time visitors may use HTTP before HSTS has been learned.
findings.fix: Redirect the HTTP entry point to HTTPS.

findings.title: No enforcing CSP header observed
findings.why: A policy can reduce browser injection impact; its presence does not establish an effective XSS defense.
findings.fix: Review a restrictive policy against your application; deploy in report-only mode first when needed.

findings.title: No framing policy observed
findings.why: A framing policy can reduce clickjacking; presence does not establish restrictive or valid values. Wildcards may intentionally permit embedding.
findings.fix: Review an appropriate CSP frame-ancestors policy if this page should not be embedded.

findings.title: MIME sniffing protection not observed
findings.why: The nosniff header helps browsers honor declared MIME types. Missing it alone is not a demonstrated exploit.
findings.fix: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and serve accurate content types.

findings.title: HTTPS connection established
evidence: TLS protocol: TLSv1.3; certificate issuer: SSL Corporation; expires: Dec 25 22:56:35 2026 GMT.
findings.why: HTTPS protects traffic in transit. TLS trust and hostname checks are enforced by the HTTP client.
findings.fix: Serve the page over HTTPS with a valid certificate; redirect HTTP entry points to HTTPS.

findings.title: No HTTP resource references in sampled markup
evidence: No explicit HTTP references found in the supported static attributes.
findings.why: Static attribute references are not proof of a browser request. This bounded token inspection skips raw-text bodies; it does not execute JavaScript, expand templates, decode entity-obfuscated URLs, or inspect CSS.
findings.fix: Use HTTPS resource URLs; confirm behavior in browser developer tools.

findings.title: No HTTP form actions in sampled markup
evidence: No explicit HTTP references found in the supported static attributes.
findings.why: A real HTTP form action can expose submitted data. This bounded token inspection skips raw-text bodies; it does not execute JavaScript, expand templates, decode entity-obfuscated URLs, or inspect CSS.
findings.fix: Change form actions to HTTPS and verify the submission endpoint.

findings.title: TLS certificate expiry observed
evidence: Certificate expires Dec 25 22:56:35 2026 GMT (64 days remaining).
findings.why: A certificate close to expiration can cause availability problems.
findings.fix: Verify automated certificate renewal and deployment.

findings.title: Backend vulnerability status remains unverified
evidence: No runtime inventory, authenticated scan, source code, or deployment evidence was collected.
findings.why: A public response cannot prove backend patch levels, absence of compromise, or the security of every route.
findings.fix: Collect running runtime/package versions and configuration; compare with relevant vendor advisories.

coverage.label: Public response
coverage.detail: Bounded GET requests, with public DNS validation and TLS trust enforcement.

coverage.label: Response headers and static HTML
coverage.detail: Checks apply only to the sampled response and supported HTML attributes.

coverage.label: Runtime CVEs and compromise
coverage.detail: Requires deployment evidence; version banners are unverified hints.

coverage.label: Authenticated routes and application logic
coverage.detail: No login, JavaScript execution, exploit tests, or hidden-path enumeration.

limitations: A passive posture check is not a penetration test or an all-clear.
Only the submitted page and bounded redirects were requested; no subresources or hidden paths were fetched.
Bundled banner comparison rules are a dated October 2026 snapshot, not a live vulnerability feed.
No credentials, cookie values, request bodies, or query parameters are accepted or retained.
JavaScript-generated content, CSS, authenticated areas and backend inventory are outside coverage.
